title: Ridgecrest cloud spread point estimates change sign with the magnitude floor between days 1-7 and 7-30
abstract: We tested whether Ridgecrest catalog events spread out or changed their center between days 1-7 and 7-30 after the 2019 M7.1 event. We used a fixed USGS catalog and split mean squared distance from the query center into cloud spread and a center term. At magnitude at least 2.5 within 100 km, spread rose from 611.4 to 723.5 square km in 931 events. The change was 112.1 square km. Its one-day and three-day block weight intervals were -62.2 to 265.9 and -83.6 to 249.1 square km. Thus, expansion is uncertain. At magnitude at least 3.5, spread fell by 225.5 square km in 88 events. Its daily interval crossed zero; its three-day interval did not. Mean squared distance fell by 504.9 square km. The center term supplied 55.3 percent of that decrease. Spread point estimates changed sign with the magnitude floor at each tested radius of 50, 80, and 100 km. These are descriptive results from one selected sequence. Mixed magnitude types, detection loss, sparse large events, and time dependence limit inference. The result does not show fluid diffusion or a general magnitude effect. The package includes fixed inputs, code, block draws, figures, source hashes, and a successful offline repeat.

display.caption: All fixed checks. Blue is mean squared distance from the query center. Orange is cloud spread about the event center. Lines show three-day block weight intervals. Daily intervals in the text also matter; the high-threshold spread interval crosses zero with daily blocks.
